### 📓 Docs Drift Check
This PR changes **1** package(s): `@objectstack/scenarios`, touching **104** documentable anchor(s). ⚠️ **1** changed file(s) yielded no anchor (`packages/qa/scenarios/README.md`), so the pages documenting them are **NOT COVERED by this run** — this is not a clean bill of health for those files.

**16** hand-written doc(s) name something this change touched — list omitted above 15 rows. Re-derive on the tree named below: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 3bbda33b78fff2681db9c09732347bc62ffc4cc6`.

⛔ **9** release-owned page(s) also affected — read-only, see AGENTS.md Documentation Guardrails.

<details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- **1** changed file(s) yielded no anchor (`packages/qa/scenarios/README.md`) — pages documenting those are invisible to this run
- **35** name(s) were too generic to anchor anything (single lowercase words)
- the SDK route bridge reached **65** of **247** client-bound route-ledger rows — the other **182** have no registrar `path:` tail to select them, so pages documenting THEIR client methods cannot appear above, on this or any run. Of those **182**: **0** are remediable by widening that discovery convention (an in-repo file declares the path; the convention did not scan it); **59** are structural — on a ledger where NOT ONE row is declared in-repo, so no discovery change reaches them at any price; **123** are undecided (no in-repo declaration, on a ledger that has other in-repo registrars — absence and an unreadable spelling are not distinguishable here). The rows themselves: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --bridge-coverage`
- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **1** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 3bbda33b78fff2681db9c09732347bc62ffc4cc6` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

<details><summary>Which tree this was computed on</summary>

This run read `content/docs` from `3d2d3fec09dee811db05edec246b527e7899e941` — the merge of head `372dfc5ec31481488d0c6961da5654cc0be6f44f` into base `3bbda33b78fff2681db9c09732347bc62ffc4cc6`, which is what `actions/checkout` gives a `pull_request` run. **Not** the PR head.

A worktree cut from an older `main` holds a different `content/docs`, so re-deriving there can legitimately return a different list — that is a **different tree, not a wrong row**. To answer on the same tree:

```sh
# while this PR is open — GitHub drops the merge commit once it closes
git fetch origin 3d2d3fec09dee811db05edec246b527e7899e941 && git checkout 3d2d3fec09dee811db05edec246b527e7899e941
# afterwards, rebuild it from the two parents, which stay fetchable
git fetch origin 3bbda33b78fff2681db9c09732347bc62ffc4cc6 372dfc5ec31481488d0c6961da5654cc0be6f44f && git checkout -B drift-repro 3bbda33b78fff2681db9c09732347bc62ffc4cc6 && git merge --no-ff 372dfc5ec31481488d0c6961da5654cc0be6f44f

node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 3bbda33b78fff2681db9c09732347bc62ffc4cc6
```

⚠️ That checkout carried **uncommitted changes**, so the commit above does not fully identify what was read.
</details>

> Advisory only, and a **precision-first** one (#9192): a page is listed because it names a
> symbol, wire route or SDK method this diff touched — not because it mentions a changed
> package. Each row says which anchor put it there, so a wrong row is reportable rather than
> merely annoying. To re-verify, run the `docs-accuracy-audit` workflow scoped to these files:
> `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs 3bbda33b78fff2681db9c09732347bc62ffc4cc6` → pass the list as
> `args.docs`, on the commit named under **Which tree this was computed on**.

## Contract review

Served-tier: `TIER_DEFAULT`
Head-sha: `e11c9fe8dca02f1151fbee41a0100271c10f1665`
Local-runs: none

### ① Derived judgments

Read against `exports` (`.`, `./score`, `./score/full`, `./runner`, `./export`) and `bin`, diff `6dd57163..e11c9fe8`.
- Every new export reachable through a subpath barrel is named. `datasets.ts`, `ask-skills.ts` and `cli.ts` are re-exported by no barrel, so they are correctly not counted.
- The widening is additive. Both card keys are optional, and `checkDatasets` does nothing when a card has neither, so the seven untouched cards stay valid. The new record half and scorecard row appear only on a card that declares the keys. With the flag off, the argv is unchanged. `--ask-skills` is refused on the codex, external and `recorded:` drivers.
- Subscription-only holds. Ask turns still run on `turnEnv()`, which strips `API_BILLING_ENV`, and the constructor still runs `assertSubscriptionLogin`. Skills are written only under `.claude/skills/NAME/`, and symlinks are skipped. No path runs on an API key.
- **should-fix:** a skill's front matter (`allowed-tools`, `model`) can widen an ask turn beyond `mcp__app`, because the ask argv sets no `--tools`. Only the sha256 records this. Refuse those keys, or pin the tool set.
- **should-fix:** replaying a pre-PR recording of either changed card throws `MissingRecordingError` on each `dq_*` step. Those asks count as failed, not as not measured. State this in the changeset, or classify the error as not measured.
- **nit:** the declaration does not name `scoreCardArtifact` or `artifactToEvalGraph`, though both change behaviour. `AskSkillsInfo` can be reached through `DriverInfo.askSkills` but has no exported name.

### ② Semver level

`patch` on `@objectstack/scenarios`. The `Clause-②: yes (widening)` and `Metadata-protocol: none` lines match the PR body byte for byte, and both are correct: the card format is a devx format, not platform metadata, and a non-protocol widening ships `patch`. This agrees with claim 6946793040.

### ③ Boundary flags

- The dev's `open_questions` list is empty. Both out-of-scope notes are stated in the PR body. Accepted.
- E2 was re-ruled to A. The near-miss grader needs no code change once `candidates` lands, and the round stays on the card.
- SQL push-down: no query path is touched.
- Check-runs: every completed run is success or skipped. Pending: Test Core 1, 2 and 4 of 10 are in progress, and 8 to 10 plus the required `Test Core` aggregate are not posted yet.

## Contract review

Served-tier: `TIER_DEFAULT`
Head-sha: `372dfc5ec31481488d0c6961da5654cc0be6f44f`
Local-runs: none

### ① Derived judgments

Delta review of `e11c9fe8..372dfc5e`: three commits, six files, no main merge. It answers record 6947085760.
- **S1 closed.** `frontMatterRefusal` holds every `SKILL.md`, nested ones included, to ten keys, and runs in the constructor before any process starts. Edge cases:
  - Refused: an unknown key, a known key in another case (`Allowed-Tools`), a quoted, flow, `?` or `<<` key, and an indented line under no key.
  - Refused: a block that opens late, opens with a space, or never closes. A sloppy close only makes the reader scan more lines, so the worst case is a false refusal, never a missed key.
  - Accepted: a key nested under `metadata`, which the session ignores, and a file with no front matter, which declares nothing.
  - CRLF, a lone CR and a BOM are handled.
- **S2 closed.** `MissingRecordingError` on a dataset question now sets `notMeasured`, which `datasetTally` leaves out of the total. If every ask is unrecorded the row is `0/0`, which reads `not-run`, never `pass`. Live drivers never throw this error. A new pin covers the pre-PR replay case.
- **Nit closed.** The changeset now names `scoreCardArtifact`, `artifactToEvalGraph` and `AskSkillsInfo`.
- **nit (new):** `RecordingDriver` records no turn when a live ask throws. A replay then turns that counted failure into not measured, so a row can rise from 4/5 live to 4/4 on replay. Plain questions still count it as an error. It is rare, because `ClaudeCodeDriver.ask` returns rather than throws.
- **nit (new):** the file match is case-sensitive. On a case-insensitive filesystem, a top-level lowercase `skill.md` crashes with a TypeError instead of a refusal. A nested one goes unchecked, but an ask turn has no file tools to reach it.

### ② Semver level

Unchanged: `patch`, `Clause-②: yes (widening)`, `Metadata-protocol: none`. The line is byte-identical in the changeset and the PR body (diffed). The delta adds only refusals on the opt-in flag.

### ③ Boundary flags

- The dev's one open question (who patches the PR body) is answered: the body now carries the resolutions.
- The HTML-signature note is accepted. It does not affect the contract.
- SQL push-down: no query path is touched.
- Check-runs: 37 success and 18 skipped, none pending. All eleven required contexts are green or skipped by their own rules, including `Test Core`.

Implemented-by: `claude/issue-34687-ask-skills-dataset-cards`
Reviewed-by: `session_01WGufzgh1zkZzDXL36ckWAG`

**VERDICT: PASS**

## L1: ACCEPT · 2026-11-17T12:42Z

Head-sha: 372dfc5ec31481488d0c6961da5654cc0be6f44f
Reviewer: seat 3 L1-c, for card #34687 (claim restated 6946793040, seat L2 PASS 6947085760 at e11c9fe8, fix-round-2 report 6948219525).

### 席位核对

**PR shape.** Draft, base `main`, `Part of #34687`, with no closing verb. That is right, because the card's five-repetition round with and without skills is still owed after this lands. Nine commits; fix round 2 is `a0e5047d`..`372dfc5e` (6 files, +167/-9).

**Scope vs claim.** All 27 paths sit inside the restated claim's surface: `packages/qa/scenarios/**` (src, tests, README), `docs/qa/scenarios/{README.md,order_to_cash.json,travel_expense.json}` and one changeset. `invoice_with_line_items` is left alone, and the body gives the reason (its `expect` is corpus-derived, outside the surface).

**Declaration.** The body's `Clause-②: yes (widening)` line and the changeset's line read the same, including the nit-round additions (`scoreCardArtifact` and `artifactToEvalGraph` answering differently; `AskSkillsInfo` unexported). `Metadata-protocol: none`. The changeset names `@objectstack/scenarios` only, at `patch`, which is right for `none`. No other package's `src/**` moved. The narrow import graph's new `@objectstack/spec/ui` edge is a consumer read of `DatasetSchema` / `normalizeDatasetTerm`, not a spec change.

**Governed / size.** `check-governed-merges --pr 34808`: 0 of 27 paths, NOT governed, 1905 lines (under 3000).

**Check-runs at 372dfc5e.** 55 runs, every one `success` or `skipped`: `Lint & Repo Gates`, `TypeScript Type Check`, `Test Core` and all 10 shards, `Check Changeset` (both runs), `PR-body guards` (both runs), `Governed Surface Queue Guard`, `Check Documentation Links`, `Live E2E UI`. The UI legs were skipped by path filter.

**S1 of L2 (a skill's front matter widening the turn): closed.** I read `frontMatterRefusal` against the ways a reader could see fewer keys than the CLI does:
- It requires a bare `---` on line 1 (BOM and CRLF stripped).
- It closes on the first exact `---`. Any looser close the CLI might use (trailing space, `...`) can only end the block earlier, which means fewer keys, so the reader errs toward refusing.
- It refuses quoted, flow, `?` and indented-orphan lines.
- It checks every nested `SKILL.md`.

A key outside the ten-key set never reaches a turn. With no `--permission-mode` on the ask argv, a body ``!`cmd` `` still has no Bash grant, so the closed set plus `--allowedTools mcp__app Skill` is the whole widening story. Pins: six refused keys, nested file, six unsure-read shapes, an accepted CRLF and comment block with `metadata.allowed-tools` nested, and the constructor refusal. Ablation is recorded in 6948219525.

**S2 of L2 (pre-PR recording replays fail every `dq_*`): closed.** A `MissingRecordingError` on a dataset question sets `notMeasured`, never `error`. The replay pin records a real run without dataset questions, replays it against the dataset card, and asserts `0/0 · 2 not measured` with the ordinary questions' grades unchanged. A missing recording for an ordinary question still throws as before.

**Code read (graders, loader, driver).**
- `metric-selected` reads `provenance.kind/dataset.name/measures[].name`, which match `DatasetProvenanceSchema` (packages/spec/src/ai/dataset-tools.zod.ts:234), and never the arguments.
- `fallback-labelled` keys on `input.objectName`, the MCP door's argument name, and on `OBJECT_QUERY_TOOLS`, which unions the door's three tools with `OBJECT_QUERY_SOURCE_TOOL_NAMES`.
- The loader imports `DatasetSchema` and `normalizeDatasetTerm` rather than restating them. It holds every card word to D3 (exact hit, the ambiguous set, near-miss as no hit plus substring) and refuses a dataset-question id that collides with a question or operation id (they share the replay step segment).
- `datasetQuestionPrompt` carries the ask, today, and "answer from the app's data". It carries no answer format and no route hint.
- With the option off, the ask argv is unchanged (the existing pin stays green).

**Docs made false?** Both READMEs gain their rows. The `Never summed silently` sentence names the new `ask skills` dimension. `.claude/skills/scenario-eval/**` does not restate the table dimensions or the ask argv, so nothing there turns false.

### Must-fix
None.

### Should-fix
- **S1. `asked-back:no-figure` fails a reply that counts its candidates.** `statedFigures` drops list numbering and dates, but not a numeral that counts the options. "I found 2 metrics that match 'revenue': Booked amount or Billed amount — which one?" and 「营收对应 2 个指标…您是指哪一个？」 are correct ask-backs, and both fail on `2`. A year written alone ("revenue in 2026?") fails the same way. This is a plausible model phrasing, so it will show up in the round as false fails on the ambiguous rows. It can be closed in either of two ways:
  - Drop a bare integer that reads as a count of options (for example, followed within a word or two by metric/measure/reading/option/指标/口径/种/个), and pin both languages.
  - Or name this shape in the README's grader paragraph and have the round read `no-figure` misses by hand, as the body already says for the `fallback-labelled` label list.

  Either is fine. If the second, the carrier is the #34687 round, not a new card.

### Notes
- N1. A `SKILL.md` whose front-matter `name` differs from its directory is listed by the session under the front-matter name. The record (`askSkills[].name`) states the directory name, while the `loaded skill …` note states what the transcript called. Today's pilot skill has them equal, so this is only worth a line if a pack ever diverges.
- N2. `skillVersionOf` matches an indented `version:` at any depth inside the block, not only top level or `metadata.version` as its doc says (for example, `compatibility:\n  version: …`). It is record text only.
- N3. The near-miss rows (`dq_booking_total`, `dq_claimed_so_far`) grade an ask-back. A D3-rule-4-faithful agent without the skill, and before #34761/#34763 add `candidates`, would answer with a labelled fallback and fail them. That is the comparison the round is for, and the README says what each grader reads, but the round's write-up should not read those baseline misses as agent faults.

Next: the seat owes the L2 delta on `a0e5047d`..`372dfc5e` (S1, S2 and the Clause-② nit) before o3-F lands. A later push owes an L1-c delta read.
